example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]は足[あし]が速[はや]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: A flexed arm pushing: power and strength.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at this single stroke and picture a bent arm flexing with <radical>power</radical> — the elbow cocked, the muscle bulging. That one flexed arm is all you need to see: that's <kanji>power</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A weightlifter named Rio steps up to the bar and gives a warrior's yell as she flexes: "<reading>りょく</reading>!" The whole gym feels the raw strength in that shout.
items.description: 力 and 九 are both two strokes with a hook, and the hooks point opposite ways. 力 starts with a flat horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left, with a slash cutting through it. 九 starts with a short slash, then a stroke that curves right and flicks upward.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男の人は力が強いですね。
example_sentences.english: That man is strong, isn't he?
example_sentences.furigana: あの男[おとこ]の人[ひと]は力[ちから]が強[つよ]いですね。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖父は力が弱いです。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather doesn't have much strength.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の祖[そ]父[ふ]は力[ちから]が弱[よわ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: テーブルが重いですから、一緒に力を使いましょう。
example_sentences.english: The table is heavy, so let's use our strength together.
example_sentences.furigana: テーブルが重[おも]いですから、一[いっ]緒[しょ]に力[ちから]を使[つか]いましょう。

items.mnemonic_text: A sprout pushing up from the ground: life and birth.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a single seed pushed into the <radical>earth</radical> — that cross of soil where everything begins. A green shoot cracks through and reaches up out of the ground. From that patch of earth, something new is born: this is <kanji>life</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei, the star student, is the first sprout to shoot up every spring, hand raised before anyone else has even woken. When the teacher asks who's most full of life, Sei（<reading>せい</reading>）is already standing, beaming.
items.description: Means "life" or "birth"; a very common kanji that shows up in words about living, being born, students, and fresh or raw things.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、駅で先生に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met my teacher at the station yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、駅[えき]で先[せん]生[せい]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 学生は毎日図書館で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: Students read books at the library every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 学[がく]生[せい]は毎[まい]日[にち]図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 去年、妹が生まれました。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister was born last year.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]、妹[いもうと]が生[う]まれました。

items.mnemonic_text: In the evening (夕) you call out a mouth's (口) name.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In the <radical>evening</radical> nobody can see your face, so your <radical>mouth</radical> has to give your <kanji>name</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A performer named Mei struts into Koichi's konbini and belts out "<reading>めい</reading>, that's my name, don't wear it out!" She spells it letter by letter until the whole shop knows exactly who she is.
items.description: 名 and 多 both start with the same slanted three-stroke piece. 名 finishes with a small closed box beneath it. 多 repeats that slanted piece a second time instead, so it is one shape stacked twice.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の名前は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What is the teacher's name?
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の名[な]前[まえ]は何[なに]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は有名な医者です。
example_sentences.english: He is a famous doctor.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は有[ゆう]名[めい]な医[い]者[しゃ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あの映画は有名です。
example_sentences.english: That movie is famous.
example_sentences.furigana: あの映[えい]画[が]は有[ゆう]名[めい]です。

items.mnemonic_text: A person carrying grain across one full year.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>slash</radical> cut into the <radical>shield</radical> after each harvest counts off one more <kanji>year</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A tired farmer counts the passing seasons by taking a nap in the shade of that scarecrow each time the harvest ends. He mumbles "<reading>ねん</reading>、ねん" — like the sleepy sound of nodding off — once for every year that rolls by.
items.description: Means "year"; a very common kanji appearing in dates, ages, and words about time.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年、海に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went to the sea last year.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]、海[うみ]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 今年、新しいパソコンを買います。
example_sentences.english: I will buy a new computer this year.
example_sentences.furigana: 今年[ことし]、新[あたら]しいパソコンを買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、兄は大学に行きます。
example_sentences.english: My older brother will go to university next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、兄[あに]は大[だい]学[がく]に行[い]きます。

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) at the temple (寺) marks the hour.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> crossing the <radical>Buddhist temple</radical> roof is how the whole village used to tell the <kanji>time</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cheerful clockmaker named Jiro keeps every timepiece in Koichi's konbini ticking, and each hour on the hour he shouts "<reading>じ</reading>! じ!" as the alarms go off. Whenever you need to know the time, you listen for Jiro's じ.
items.description: Means time or hour, and shows up everywhere you talk about clock time and telling the hour.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は何時ですか。
example_sentences.english: What time is it now?
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]は何[なん]時[じ]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい時計を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new watch.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい時計[とけい]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 時々友達と映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I sometimes watch movies with friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 時[とき]々[どき]友[とも]達[だち]と映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) seen through a gate (門): the space in between.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a <radical>gate</radical> with its two swinging doors thrown open. Right in the gap between them, the <radical>sun</radical> is hanging low, filling the opening with light. That sliver of sun caught in the gate is the space between things — an interval, the gap <kanji>between</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A guard named Kan stands watch in that gateway, timing exactly how long the sun lingers in the gap. Every time the interval passes he shouts "<reading>かん</reading>!" and slams one door shut.
items.description: 間 and 聞 are the same gate frame with different contents. 間 sets 日, the sun, inside the gateway. 聞 stands an ear there instead. What is framed by the gate settles it every time.

example_sentences.japanese: 病院はデパートと駅の間です。
example_sentences.english: The hospital is between the department store and the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 病[びょう]院[いん]はデパートと駅[えき]の間[あいだ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 二時間テレビを見ました。
example_sentences.english: I watched TV for two hours.
example_sentences.furigana: 二[に]時[じ]間[かん]テレビを見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 三週間待ちました。
example_sentences.english: I waited for three weeks.
example_sentences.furigana: 三[さん]週[しゅう]間[かん]待[ま]ちました。

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) with wings and birds: naming each day of the week.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>pheasant</radical> that only calls when the <radical>sun</radical> is properly up marks off another <kanji>weekday</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Yoko, exhausted, groans "no more, no more" as she crosses off day after day on the wall calendar. Every square she reaches she moans <reading>よう</reading>, よう, because to her every single weekday feels the same.

example_sentences.japanese: 水曜日にデパートで新しい靴を買います。
example_sentences.english: I will buy new shoes at the department store on Wednesday.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[すい]曜[よう]日[ひ]にデパートで新[あたら]しい靴[くつ]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 金曜日の夜は楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: Friday night is fun.
example_sentences.furigana: 金[きん]曜[よう]日[ひ]の夜[よる]は楽[たの]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日に公園で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I read books in the park on Sundays.
example_sentences.furigana: 日[にち]曜[よう]日[ひ]に公[こう]園[えん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

items.mnemonic_text: A roof over a moment held in the hand: now.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>One</radical> <radical>person</radical> under a roof with no plan past this evening is living entirely in the <kanji>now</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Right now, this very second, Koichi is slamming down onigiri prices at the konbini and yelling "<reading>こん</reading>!" like a battle cry to get you buying before the moment passes. Every time you hear こん, you know it means now, now, now.
items.description: 今 and 会 wear the same wide roof. Under it 今 has only a short stroke and a small hook. 会 packs a fuller body beneath the roof, with a horizontal bar and legs below it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、私は忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: I am busy right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]、私[わたし]は忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、友達が家に来ます。
example_sentences.english: A friend is coming to my house today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、友[とも]達[だち]が家[いえ]に来[き]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今週、映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I will watch a movie this week.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[こん]週[しゅう]、映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

items.mnemonic_text: Making a lap around the calendar road: one week.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a boxy calendar page laid flat, with a winding <radical>road</radical> threading across it, square to square. You put your footsteps down and <radical>advance</radical> one box at a time. The road curves right back to where it started. One full loop around that grid — that's one <kanji>week</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A woman named Shu (<reading>しゅう</reading>) plans her whole week on that looping calendar path, and every seven days she sighs "しゅう, another one done!" as she starts the loop again. Hear her say しゅう each time the week resets.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に友達と遊びます。
example_sentences.english: I play with my friends on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に友[とも]達[だち]と遊[あそ]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 来週は忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: I am busy next week.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]週[しゅう]は忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先週、新しい本を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new book last week.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]週[しゅう]、新[あたら]しい本[ほん]を買[か]いました。

items.mnemonic_text: A person over a mother figure repeating every time.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>chevron</radical> on the sign with <radical>do not</radical> underneath it turns up at <kanji>every</kanji> single corner in town.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clock belongs to Mai, who winds it every morning and shouts "My time!" as it rings. Hear her name <reading>まい</reading> as the sound that hammers home the routine — every day, まい, まい, まい.
items.description: Means "every" and shows up in common time words for recurring events, such as every day, every week, and every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日コーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink coffee every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]コーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は毎晩本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: My father reads a book every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月図書館に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to the library every month.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]月[つき]図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]に行[い]きます。

items.mnemonic_text: A shape split evenly down the middle: half.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two matchsticks lie crossed on the counter, making that <radical>ten</radical> mark. A cleaver comes straight down through the middle. What's left is two legs, kicked out evenly, each side mirroring the other. Ten cut clean down the centre, split into equal parts — that's <kanji>half</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Han, the half-and-half chef, holds up a plate. One side is rice, the other is curry, split exactly down the center. "<reading>はん</reading>!" he barks, tapping the dividing line. To Han, half is the only portion worth serving.
items.description: 半 and 羊 both sit horizontal bars on a vertical under a split top. Count the bars: 半 has two, 羊 has three. That extra horizontal is the only reliable difference.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日二時間半勉強します。
example_sentences.english: I study for two and a half hours every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]二[に]時[じ]間[かん]半[はん]勉[べん]強[きょう]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこのパンを半分食べます。
example_sentences.english: I will eat half of this bread.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はこのパンを半[はん]分[ぶん]食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 本の半分を読みました。
example_sentences.english: I read half of the book.
example_sentences.furigana: 本[ほん]の半[はん]分[ぶん]を読[よ]みました。

items.mnemonic_text: A sword (刀) dividing something into parts and minutes.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The woodcutter prises a chipped <radical>sword</radical> out of its frozen rice cake and wipes it clean. She gives it one job: split a log. It comes down clean, and the two halves lean apart into a fresh <radical>eight</radical>. One <kanji>minute</kanji>, one cut, and the sword finally earns its keep.
items.reading_mnemonic: The woodcutter, sawdust in her eyebrows, times herself at one log a minute and calls it the most <reading>fun</reading> you can have before breakfast. The sword, back in her hands and still chipped, snorts <reading>ふん</reading> — it was the one doing all the work.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand this book.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: パンを半分食べました。
example_sentences.english: I ate half of the bread.
example_sentences.furigana: パンを半[はん]分[ぶん]食[た]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で五分待ちました。
example_sentences.english: I waited for five minutes at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で五[ご]分[ふん]待[ま]ちました。

items.mnemonic_text: A child (子) under a roof of scattered ideas: study.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>small</radical> <radical>child</radical> under a <radical>cover</radical> with nothing to do but turn pages is going to <kanji>study</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the school, the star pupil Gaku is the one who never stops studying, and everyone in the echoing hallways calls out <reading>がく</reading> whenever they need the answer. Hear がく and you hear the kid who lives to learn.
items.description: Means study or learning; a very common kanji that shows up in words for student, school, and academic subjects.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は学生です。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister is a student.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to school tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 数学は難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Math is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 数[すう]学[がく]は難[むずか]しいです。

items.mnemonic_text: A tree (木) crossed with mingling students: a school.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>tree</radical> in a yard where children <radical>mingle</radical> between two bells is standing in a <kanji>school</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, has set up a pop-up shop right inside the school gate, restocking onigiri between classes and muttering <reading>こう</reading>, こう as he lines up the shelves. The kids buy their lunch from him before the bell.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日学校へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to school every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]学[がっ]校[こう]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 校庭に犬がいます。
example_sentences.english: There is a dog in the schoolyard.
example_sentences.furigana: 校[こう]庭[てい]に犬[いぬ]がいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、学校を休みます。
example_sentences.english: I will take a day off from school today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、学[がっ]校[こう]を休[やす]みます。

items.mnemonic_text: A person stepping ahead of the rest: previous and first.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A pair of <radical>human legs</radical> with one foot already out past the body is a step <kanji>ahead</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Those bodiless legs sprint down the mountain trail so far ahead they trip a wire. They set off a whole line of fireworks — <reading>せん</reading>, せん, せん — bursting one after another. That marks how far in front they already are.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、先生に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met the teacher yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、先[せん]生[せい]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先週、友達と一緒に映画を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I watched a movie with a friend last week.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]週[しゅう]、友[とも]達[だち]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先月、新しい靴を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought new shoes last month.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]月[げつ]、新[あたら]しい靴[くつ]を買[か]いました。

items.mnemonic_text: Speech (言) with a mouth counting to five (五): words and language.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A waterfall of <radical>speech</radical> pours down into a waiting <radical>mouth</radical> below. The mouth swallows every word whole without chewing once. Stuffed with so many words, it finally speaks a whole <kanji>language</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Behind the beeping till at Koichi's konbini, a chatty regular named Go won't stop talking. Every single language pours out of him at once, and the only word you catch is his own name: <reading>ご</reading>, ご, ご.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と日本語で話します。
example_sentences.english: I speak with my friend in Japanese.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と日本[にほん]語[ご]で話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: この本は英語です。
example_sentences.english: This book is in English.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は英[えい]語[ご]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日日本語を勉強します。
example_sentences.english: I study Japanese every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]日本[にほん]語[ご]を勉[べん]強[きょう]します。

items.mnemonic_text: Speech (言) plus a tongue (舌): telling a story.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> releasing stacked lines of <radical>speech</radical> leans in close, and right beside it a <radical>tongue</radical> sticks out of a mouth, wagging nonstop. Put the speech next to the busy tongue and you've got someone who just won't stop talking, spinning story after <kanji>story</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Wanda the storyteller loves an audience, so she waves both hands and calls out "<reading>わ</reading>!" every time she starts a new tale. That little "わ" is her signal that another long talk is about to begin.
items.description: Means talk or story; shows up in everyday words for speaking, conversation, and telephone.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、友達と話します。
example_sentences.english: I will talk with my friend tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、友[とも]達[だち]と話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい電話を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new phone.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい電[でん]話[わ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の話は面白いです。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's story is interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の話[はなし]は面[おも]白[しろ]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: Words (言) sold (売) to your eyes: reading.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Somebody has to <radical>sell</radical> you the <radical>words</radical> before you can sit down anywhere and <kanji>read</kanji> them.
items.reading_mnemonic: The reader you find hunched over those lines of speech is a poison-pen critic, and you nickname her Doku (<reading>どく</reading>) because every review she reads she then tears apart. Watch her read a page and you can practically see the どく venom drip off her pen.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I read books every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日本[にほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で面白い雑誌を読みました。
example_sentences.english: I read an interesting magazine at the library.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で面[おも]白[しろ]い雑[ざっ]誌[し]を読[よ]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がその手紙を読みましたか。
example_sentences.english: Who read that letter?
example_sentences.furigana: 誰[だれ]がその手[て]紙[がみ]を読[よ]みましたか。

items.mnemonic_text: A brush (聿) laid over a sunny page: writing.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>brush</radical> moving all <radical>day</radical> with nothing to show for it but marks means somebody had to <kanji>write</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa, the fire-breathing crow, lands on your notebook and squints at your terrible handwriting, muttering "<reading>しょ</reading>, しょ" every time you smudge a letter. Each little puff of flame dries the ink so you can keep writing.
items.description: Means "write"; shows up in words about writing, documents, and books, like 書く (to write).

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I will read a book at the library.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に手紙を書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a letter to a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: かばんに辞書を入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put the dictionary in my bag.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんに辞[じ]書[しょ]を入[い]れました。

items.mnemonic_text: An ear (耳) inside the gate (門): listening for who is there.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>ear</radical> pressed to the crack in the <radical>gate</radical> is there for one reason, which is to <kanji>hear</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Mon-Bun, the scholarly rabbit twins, press their ears to the gate to hear you ask a question. They immediately start arguing about the answer. "<reading>ぶん</reading>!" they squeak in unison. Those two never agree on anything they overhear.
items.description: 聞 and 間 are the same gate frame with different things standing inside it. 聞 puts 耳, an ear, in the gateway. 間 frames the sun there instead. What the gate contains is the whole difference.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝ラジオを聞きます。
example_sentences.english: I listen to the radio every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]ラジオを聞[き]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は朝、新聞を読みます。
example_sentences.english: My father reads the newspaper in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は朝[あさ]、新[しん]聞[ぶん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 鳥の声が聞こえます。
example_sentences.english: I can hear birds singing.
example_sentences.furigana: 鳥[とり]の声[こえ]が聞[き]こえます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> is caught low in a <radical>cross</radical>-braced frame on the left, still climbing, while the <radical>moon</radical> on the right has not gone down. Both are up at once, for twenty minutes a day: <kanji>morning</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Chou is the long-distance runner who is out before anybody else, and she stretches her greeting the whole length of the street as she passes your window — a long, unreasonably cheerful 「<reading>ちょう</reading>」. If you hear ちょう, the moon is still up.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝六時に起きます。
example_sentences.english: I get up at six every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]六[ろく]時[じ]に起[お]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯にパンを食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat bread for breakfast.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]にパンを食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 朝、公園で犬と遊びます。
example_sentences.english: In the morning, I play with the dog in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]、公[こう]園[えん]で犬[いぬ]と遊[あそ]びます。

items.mnemonic_text: A crossroads where you choose to go.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a stick figure caught mid-stride, legs split wide, one arm swinging forward — the whole character leans into the <radical>step</radical>. That's a person who won't stand still, always moving to the next place. When you see this shape, you see someone about to <kanji>go</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, can't sit still either — the second a shelf goes empty he's out the door to go restock it, muttering "<reading>こう</reading>, こう, keep it moving." Wherever he needs to go, he goes at a run.
items.description: Means "go" and shows up constantly in verbs of movement and travel, such as 行く (to go).

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、銀行に行きました。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I went to the bank.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、銀[ぎん]行[こう]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 家族と飛行機で旅行します。
example_sentences.english: I will travel by airplane with my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]と飛[ひ]行[こう]機[き]で旅[りょ]行[こう]します。

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、行ってきます。
example_sentences.english: I'm off, Mom.
example_sentences.furigana: お母[かあ]さん、行[い]ってきます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>body</radical> lies flat under a <radical>drop</radical> of sweat, the <radical>sun</radical> pinned beneath it against a line of <radical>ground</radical>. No shade is left; work has stopped: the flattening middle of <kanji>daytime</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Chuu the loyal mouse will not nap through it. While every other body is flat out he stands at his post in the full sun, squeaking 「<reading>ちゅう</reading>」 on the hour so that nobody oversleeps. Absurdly devoted, ちゅう, right through the worst of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日昼ご飯を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat lunch every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼とは昼頃会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met him around noon.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]とは昼[ひる]頃[ころ]会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の昼ご飯はパンでした。
example_sentences.english: Today's lunch was bread.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]の昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]はパンでした。

items.mnemonic_text: A tree of grain drawing people to come.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a <radical>tree</radical> standing at a crossroads with two little travelers resting under its branches, one on each side of the trunk. The tree can't move, so it waves the travelers over: "<kanji>Come</kanji>! Come to me, sit in my shade." Everyone always comes to the tree.
items.reading_mnemonic: The traveler who comes to the tree is Rye, and he never arrives quietly — he shouts "<reading>らい</reading>, I'm here!" as he strolls up the path. Whenever someone comes into view down the road, listen for that らい.
items.description: 来 is 米 with an extra horizontal across the top. Count the horizontal bars: 米 has one, 来 has two.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、誰が来ますか。
example_sentences.english: Who is coming tomorrow?
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、誰[だれ]が来[き]ますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 来月、日本へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to Japan next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]、日本[にほん]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、新しい先生が来ます。
example_sentences.english: A new teacher will come next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、新[あたら]しい先[せん]生[せい]が来[き]ます。

items.mnemonic_text: A broom and a stop: sweeping up and returning home.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Putting down the <radical>knife</radical> and picking up the <radical>sweeper</radical> is what you do the hour you <kanji>return</kanji> home.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki, the tree spirit, has been out riding the wind all day, and now she giggles as she slips back inside her old tree with a soft <reading>き</reading>. Watch her return home and you'll hear that き every time.
items.description: Means "return," as in going or coming back home; the core kanji in the verb 帰る, to return.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は早く家に帰ります。
example_sentences.english: I will return home early tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は早[はや]く家[いえ]に帰[かえ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 遅いですから、一緒に帰りましょう。
example_sentences.english: It's late, so let's go home together.
example_sentences.furigana: 遅[おそ]いですから、一[いっ]緒[しょ]に帰[かえ]りましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、お帰りなさい。
example_sentences.english: Welcome back, dad!
example_sentences.furigana: お父[とう]さん、お帰[かえ]りなさい。

items.mnemonic_text: Two mountains stacked, something pushing out.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look closely and you see one <radical>mountain</radical> stacked right on top of another mountain — two sets of three peaks piled up. When the peaks get that tall, there's only one thing you want to do: get out and leave. So this doubled-up mountain means <kanji>exit</kanji>, leave.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the exit of the mountain trail stands a hiker who sneezes so hard every time someone leaves — a huge "<reading>しゅつ</reading>!" — that the whole vending machine rattles. Every time you head for the exit, you hear that "しゅつ" behind you.
items.description: Means exit or leave; shows up in everyday words about going out, leaving, and departures.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、手紙を出します。
example_sentences.english: I will send a letter tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、手[て]紙[がみ]を出[だ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、何時に家を出ますか。
example_sentences.english: What time do you leave the house every day?
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]、何[なに]時[じ]に家[いえ]を出[で]ますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の出口はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the station exit?
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の出[で]口[ぐち]はどこですか。

items.mnemonic_text: A person ducking under a doorway to enter.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Watch the shape closely: it's a little figure ducking their head as they <radical>enter</radical> through a low doorway. You lean, you dip, you step through — and just like that, you <kanji>enter</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The figure ducking through the door is a new student, and as they enter the echoing school hallway everyone whispers "the new one, <reading>にゅう</reading>, the new one." Every time someone new enters, that にゅう ripples down the hall.
items.description: 入, 人 and 八 are the same pair of strokes. In 入 the short left stroke begins partway down the long one, leaving a small overhang at the top. 人 meets at a clean point, and 八 never lets the two touch.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と一緒に店に入りました。
example_sentences.english: I entered the shop with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に店[みせ]に入[はい]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーに砂糖を入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put sugar in the coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: コーヒーに砂[さ]糖[とう]を入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の入口はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the station's entrance?
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の入[いり]口[ぐち]はどこですか。

items.mnemonic_text: An eye (目) on legs going out to see.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take an <radical>eye</radical> (目) and stand it up on a pair of <radical>human legs</radical> (儿), and suddenly it can <radical>see</radical> and walk around anywhere it wants. Where does an eye on legs go? Out into the world, to look at everything. So this is what it means to <kanji>see</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ken, the sword-collecting dog, drags you over to his wall of antique swords because he wants you to see his newest one. "<reading>けん</reading>! けん!" he barks, pawing at the blade until you finally look.
items.description: Means "see" and is the base of the common verb 見る (to see/look); it shows up constantly in everyday words about looking and watching.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日テレビを見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch TV every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]テレビを見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: ここから山が見えます。
example_sentences.english: You can see the mountain from here.
example_sentences.furigana: ここから山[やま]が見[み]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に新しい写真を見せました。
example_sentences.english: I showed the new picture to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に新[あたら]しい写[しゃ]真[しん]を見[み]せました。

items.mnemonic_text: A foot planted firmly: stop.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Divination</radical> cracks that all run into one footprint are telling you exactly where to <kanji>stop</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Right where you stopped, you hear a sharp "<reading>し</reading>!" — someone shushing you. It's the vending machine at the top of the trail, hissing "し, し" as it refuses to dispense until you stop and wait. That shushing し is the sound to hold onto.
items.description: Means "stop" and is the base of common verbs like 止まる and 止める, showing up anywhere something halts or is brought to a halt.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前にバスが止まりました。
example_sentences.english: The bus stopped in front of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]にバスが止[と]まりました。

example_sentences.japanese: ここでタクシーを止めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop the taxi here.
example_sentences.furigana: ここでタクシーを止[と]めてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い時計が止まりました。
example_sentences.english: The old clock stopped.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い時計[とけい]が止[と]まりました。

items.mnemonic_text: A person standing on the ground line: to stand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a person planted firmly on the ground, feet apart, refusing to budge — they <radical>stand</radical> there, solid and upright. That single image, a person rooted on the earth, is the whole character: to <kanji>stand</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A soldier named Ritsu snaps to attention on the mountain trail, standing so straight you could measure a wall against him. Every time someone shouts "<reading>りつ</reading>!" he stands up even taller.
items.description: Means "stand"; a common N5 kanji appearing in words about standing up, standing something upright, and establishing or setting things in place.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はドアの前に立っています。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is standing in front of the door.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]はドアの前[まえ]に立[た]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は立って、窓を開けました。
example_sentences.english: I stood up and opened the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は立[た]って、窓[まど]を開[あ]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: あそこに男の人が立っています。
example_sentences.english: A man is standing over there.
example_sentences.furigana: あそこに男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が立[た]っています。

items.mnemonic_text: Two people (人) sitting on the earth (土) under a roof.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anywhere with a <radical>shelter</radical> over it is somewhere two people can <radical>sit</radical>, so that is where they <kanji>sit</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The person who settles onto that patch of earth is Zara, and the moment she sits she lets out a long, satisfied "<reading>ざ</reading>あ" of relief. Every time you see someone plop down here, you hear Zara's ざ.
items.description: Means "sit"; shows up in words about sitting down, seats, and taking a seat.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がここに座りましたか。
example_sentences.english: Who sat here?
example_sentences.furigana: 誰[だれ]がここに座[すわ]りましたか。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫が机の下に座っています。
example_sentences.english: The cat is sitting under the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]が机[つくえ]の下[した]に座[すわ]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の隣に座りました。
example_sentences.english: I sat next to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の隣[となり]に座[すわ]りました。

items.mnemonic_text: A person (人) leaning on a tree (木): resting.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, you spot a <radical>person</radical> slumped sideways against a <radical>tree</radical>, leaning into the trunk like it's the comfiest chair in the world. A <radical>person</radical> plus the tree they're propped against — that's someone taking a well-earned <kanji>rest</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The hiker leaning on that tree lets out a huge, happy sigh — "<reading>きゅう</reading>!" — the sound of every muscle finally letting go. Every time you picture that person melting into rest, you hear that きゅう escape.
items.description: Means "rest" and shows up in everyday words for taking breaks and days off, like 休み.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、仕事を休みます。
example_sentences.english: I will take a day off from work tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、仕[し]事[ごと]を休[やす]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: ここでちょっと休みましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's rest here for a bit.
example_sentences.furigana: ここでちょっと休[やす]みましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪で学校を休みました。
example_sentences.english: I took a day off from school because of a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]で学[がっ]校[こう]を休[やす]みました。

items.mnemonic_text: A mouth releasing lines of speech: to say.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lines stacked above an open <radical>mouth</radical> are the sounds coming out of it the moment you <kanji>say</kanji> something.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, a general in full armor climbs the mossy steps and won't stop giving orders — every word out of his mouth is a barked command. The cats scatter as the general says "<reading>げん</reading>!" like it's the only word he knows.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は何と言いましたか。
example_sentences.english: What did the teacher say?
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は何[なに]と言[い]いましたか。

example_sentences.japanese: この言葉の意味が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand the meaning of this word.
example_sentences.furigana: この言[こと]葉[ば]の意[い]味[み]が分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は面白いことを言います。
example_sentences.english: He says interesting things.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は面[おも]白[しろ]いことを言[い]います。

items.mnemonic_text: A net (罒) over money (貝): buying with cash.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You spot something you want, so you reach for the cowrie <radical>shell</radical> that once worked as money. You lay that shell on the counter and slide it across. Handing over the shell-money is how you <kanji>buy</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The moment you buy your onigiri at Koichi's konbini, Kaa the fire-breathing crow swoops in and shrieks 「<reading>ばい</reading>」 as if saying "bye-bye" to your cash before you've even paid.
items.description: Means "buy," the verb 買う (to purchase); shows up constantly in shopping and everyday transactions.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、新しい本を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new book yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、新[あたら]しい本[ほん]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日に友達と買い物に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went shopping with a friend on Sunday.
example_sentences.furigana: 日[にち]曜[よう]日[ひ]に友[とも]達[だち]と買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、母とデパートで買い物します。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, I will shop at the department store with my mom.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、母[はは]とデパートで買[か]い物[もの]します。

items.mnemonic_text: Goods laid out on a stand: selling.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>samurai</radical> with a <radical>cover</radical> over his crest and his <radical>human legs</radical> behind a stall has come to <kanji>sell</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The vendor keeps yelling one thing at every customer who walks past: "Buy! <reading>ばい</reading>, ばい, one for you and one for the baby!" He'll sell to anyone who slows down, and every pitch ends on that same ばい.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に自転車を売りました。
example_sentences.english: I sold my bicycle to a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]を売[う]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで服を売っています。
example_sentences.english: They sell clothes at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートで服[ふく]を売[う]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: その車は売りません。
example_sentences.english: I will not sell that car.
example_sentences.furigana: その車[くるま]は売[う]りません。

items.mnemonic_text: A roof over a heap of good rice: food to eat.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A roof pitched over a heap of rice with two chopsticks laid across it is the sign for <kanji>eat</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cheerful line cook at Koichi's konbini slings hot lunches under the fluorescent lights, and every time a tray lands he shouts his catchphrase: <reading>しょく</reading>, しょく, come and get it! You hear しょく and your stomach knows it's time to eat.
items.description: Means eat or food; shows up in everyday words for meals, eating, and food, and as the verb "to eat."

example_sentences.japanese: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of food do you like?
example_sentences.furigana: どんな食[た]べ物[もの]が好[す]きですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 家族と一緒にレストランで食事します。
example_sentences.english: I will dine at a restaurant with my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]にレストランで食[しょく]事[じ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、パンを食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat bread every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]、パンを食[た]べます。

items.mnemonic_text: Food (食) beside a person yawning (欠) for a drink.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the left sits food and eating. On the right, a person opens their mouth wide in a <radical>yawn</radical>. But this mouth isn't tired — it's tipping a glass back, gulping something down. Food beside that gaping, thirsty mouth: that's <kanji>drink</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini a regular named Inn slaps a cold can on the beeping till and says the same thing every single day: "First, I drink!" You can hear the 「<reading>いん</reading>」 right at the front of Inn's name as he cracks it open.
items.description: Means "drink"; the everyday kanji in the verb 飲む, to drink.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink coffee every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]コーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たい飲み物が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a cold drink.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たい飲[の]み物[もの]が欲[ほ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、友達とお酒を飲みました。
example_sentences.english: I drank alcohol with my friend yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、友[とも]達[だち]とお酒[さけ]を飲[の]みました。

items.mnemonic_text: A ray of sunlight so bright it turns white.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> with one extra ray coming off the top is too bright to be any colour but <kanji>white</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The dazzling light spooks a startled hawk perched on the konbini roof; it beats its wings once and goes, <reading>はく</reading>, hacking out a cough as it flaps into the too-bright sky. Hear that はく every time you see this pure white flash.
items.description: All four are the same box with bars inside, and the top settles it. 白 caps the box with a small flick. 百 turns that cap into a full-width horizontal. 自 uses a short slash instead. 日 has no cap at all.

example_sentences.japanese: その白い靴は新しいですか。
example_sentences.english: Are those white shoes new?
example_sentences.furigana: その白[しろ]い靴[くつ]は新[あたら]しいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の映画は面白かったです。
example_sentences.english: The movie yesterday was interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]の映[えい]画[が]は面白[おもしろ]かったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の車は白です。
example_sentences.english: My car is white.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の車[くるま]は白[しろ]です。

items.mnemonic_text: The earth glowing under a big fire: red.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Earth</radical> baked until it gives up all its water turns the only colour it can, which is <kanji>red</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The guy who lit that underground fire is Seki, and he's coughing his lungs out from the smoke — a wet, rattling <reading>せき</reading> that won't stop as long as the red embers keep burning. Every time he sees red he starts up again: せき, せき, せき.
items.description: Means "red"; a common color kanji that shows up in words for the color itself and things like traffic lights.

example_sentences.japanese: あの赤ちゃんはかわいいです。
example_sentences.english: That baby is cute.
example_sentences.furigana: あの赤[あか]ちゃんはかわいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は赤い車が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a red car.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は赤[あか]い車[くるま]が欲[ほ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: そのかばんは赤です。
example_sentences.english: That bag is red.
example_sentences.furigana: そのかばんは赤[あか]です。

items.mnemonic_text: A fresh sprout over the moon: the blue-green of youth.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A tiny sprout curls up over the <radical>moon</radical> one clear night. Moonlight turns its leaves an odd <radical>blue-green</radical>, somewhere between sky and grass. That strange in-between color is what everyone calls <kanji>blue</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei, the star student, holds up a jar of blue-green ink and says the color is called 「<reading>せい</reading>」 — of course she knew it first. She's already dipping her perfect brush in before anyone else can answer.
items.description: Means blue or green (the fresh blue-green range); shows up in color words and in compounds about youth and freshness.

example_sentences.japanese: あの青いペンを借りました。
example_sentences.english: I borrowed that blue pen.
example_sentences.furigana: あの青[あお]いペンを借[か]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい青い車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new blue car.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい青[あお]い車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 青と白の服を着ます。
example_sentences.english: I will wear blue and white clothes.
example_sentences.furigana: 青[あお]と白[しろ]の服[ふく]を着[き]ます。

items.mnemonic_text: A sooty village over a fire: black with smoke.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the whole <radical>village</radical> at dusk, huddled around one big cooking fire. Smoke climbs and stains every wall <radical>black</radical>. It settles over the paddies, the packed earth, the wooden houses. The sooty village standing over that fire has turned one single colour: <kanji>black</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The soot-covered villagers cough up thick black lungfuls, hacking <reading>こく</reading>, こく into the night air. Every cough is darker than the last — that's the sound of black.
items.description: Means "black"; the everyday word for the color (くろ) and a common on'yomi こく in compounds.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の車は黒です。
example_sentences.english: My car is black.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の車[くるま]は黒[くろ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あの黒い犬はかわいいです。
example_sentences.english: That black dog is cute.
example_sentences.furigana: あの黒[くろ]い犬[いぬ]はかわいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は黒板に書きました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher wrote on the blackboard.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は黒[こく]板[ばん]に書[か]きました。

items.mnemonic_text: A tall tower with windows: high and expensive.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>lid</radical> over a <radical>mouth</radical> looking out across open <radical>prairie</radical> has been built very <kanji>tall</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, is jealous of that tall tower, so he stacks his onigiri shelves higher and higher until they're the tallest — and priciest — display in town. As the tower of rice balls wobbles, he shouts <reading>こう</reading> to warn a customer before it topples.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、高い時計を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought an expensive watch yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、高[たか]い時計[とけい]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの山は高いです。
example_sentences.english: That mountain over there is tall.
example_sentences.furigana: あの山[やま]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランの肉は高いです。
example_sentences.english: The meat at that restaurant is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: あのレストランの肉[にく]は高[たか]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) safe under a roof: peaceful and cheap.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a <radical>woman</radical> kneeling gracefully inside a snug little house, the <radical>roof</radical> pulled down over her like a blanket. Nothing can reach her in here — she is safe, the rent is nothing, everything is calm. A woman tucked safely under a roof is cheap and <kanji>peaceful</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: She's spreading sweet red <reading>あん</reading> (bean paste) on a bun, humming, utterly at peace. Every bite is cheap comfort — say あん and taste that calm.
items.description: 安 means cheap or peaceful, and shows up in words for low prices, safety, and being at ease.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This book is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランは安くておいしいです。
example_sentences.english: That restaurant is cheap and delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: あのレストランは安[やす]くておいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、安い靴を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought cheap shoes yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、安[やす]い靴[くつ]を買[か]いました。

items.mnemonic_text: A standing tree cut by an axe (斤): freshly new.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>axe</radical> taken to a <radical>tree</radical> that used to <radical>stand</radical> there leaves you timber that is completely <kanji>new</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The showroom greeter is Shin, and every time a new model rolls in he shouts his own name — <reading>しん</reading>! — as he yanks the cover off. Whatever Shin unveils is always brand new.
items.description: Means "new"; a very common kanji appearing in words for new things, newspapers, and freshness.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new car.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は毎朝新聞を読みます。
example_sentences.english: My father reads the newspaper every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]新[しん]聞[ぶん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: あの新しいレストランはおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: That new restaurant is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: あの新[あたら]しいレストランはおいしいです。

items.mnemonic_text: Ten (十) mouths (口) of stories passed down: old.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> counts slowly to <radical>ten</radical> every single morning. It has counted so many mornings that the counting itself feels ancient. Something repeated this many times can only be <kanji>old</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi finds an ancient rice ball at the very back of his konbini shelf, so far past its date the wrapper has yellowed. He picks it up, sighs, and mutters just one syllable at how old it is: 「<reading>こ</reading>」.
items.description: Means "old," as in old and worn from age; appears in words about age and antiquity and in the common word for "used/secondhand."

example_sentences.japanese: 古い車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought an old car.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この町には古い家がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of old houses in this town.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]には古[ふる]い家[いえ]がたくさんあります。

example_sentences.japanese: その時計は少し古いです。
example_sentences.english: That watch is a little old.
example_sentences.furigana: その時計[とけい]は少[すこ]し古[ふる]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: Two evenings (夕) stacked: many days piling up.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One <radical>evening</radical> stacked straight on top of another <radical>evening</radical> is how you end up with <kanji>many</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, Ta counts the coins in the improbable vending machine. There are far too many to hold. "<reading>た</reading>, た, た," she taps each one as they spill from her hands. There are just too many.
items.description: 多 is the same slanted piece written twice, one stacked below the other. 名 writes that piece once and puts a small closed box underneath it instead.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏はこの公園に人が多いです。
example_sentences.english: This park gets crowded in the summer.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]はこの公[こう]園[えん]に人[ひと]が多[おお]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は多分今日会社を休みます。
example_sentences.english: He's probably taking the day off work today.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は多[た]分[ぶん]今日[きょう]会[かい]社[しゃ]を休[やす]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今週は宿題が多くて大変です。
example_sentences.english: There's so much homework this week that it's rough.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[こん]週[しゅう]は宿[しゅく]題[だい]が多[おお]くて大[たい]変[へん]です。

items.mnemonic_text: Small (小) with a slash taken off: even fewer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take something <radical>small</radical> — that hook with two flanking dots — and slice one more dot away with a downward stroke. Now there's even less than small: barely anything left. When you take a bite out of small, what remains is <kanji>few</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sho, the tiny stage magician, opens his white-gloved hand to reveal only a few crumbs of confetti — "<reading>しょう</reading> time!" he squeaks, and even the doves look unimpressed by how little there is. His whole act, like everything about him, is small and few.
items.description: 少 is 小 with one extra stroke: a slash sweeping down and to the left below the base. Take that tail away and you are back to 小.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は少し寒いです。
example_sentences.english: It's a little cold today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は少[すこ]し寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: この本は少し高いです。
example_sentences.english: This book is a little expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は少[すこ]し高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を少し話します。
example_sentences.english: I speak a little Japanese.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]を少[すこ]し話[はな]します。

items.mnemonic_text: Flowing long hair on an elder: long and the eldest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hair falling well past the shoulders with one stroke trailing off the bottom of it is unmistakably <kanji>long</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: That long-bearded elder is the leader of a whole troupe of butterflies, and he lets one land on his flowing hair — a <reading>ちょう</reading> (butterfly). Every time you see this kanji, picture the ちょう resting on the leader's long locks.
items.description: Means long or leader; shows up in words for length, seniority, and being the head of something, like a school principal or a company chief.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の髪は長いです。
example_sentences.english: Her hair is long.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]の髪[かみ]は長[なが]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は長い手紙を書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a long letter.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は長[なが]い手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の話は長いです。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's stories are long.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の話[はなし]は長[なが]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) already up over the ground (十): early.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> is barely <radical>ten</radical> fingers above the horizon, which means you are up <kanji>early</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: There's a rooster at Grandma Kane's shrine who crows the moment the sun peeks over the mossy steps, way too early: "<reading>そう</reading>! そう!" he screams, so loud the cats scatter. Now you're up before dawn whether you like it or not.
items.description: Means "early" or "fast," and shows up in everyday words about time and speed like 早い (early/fast) and 早く (quickly).

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は早く起きました。
example_sentences.english: I woke up early today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は早[はや]く起[お]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は早いから、寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I have an early start tomorrow, so I'm going to sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は早[はや]いから、寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日早く学校へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to school early every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]早[はや]く学[がっ]校[こう]へ行[い]きます。

items.mnemonic_text: A jewel (玉) enclosed by borders: a country.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>jewel</radical> kept inside an <radical>enclosure</radical> that nobody may cross is what makes a <kanji>country</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the border of this walled country stands a guard named Koku, who stamps every passport with a cheerful <reading>こく</reading> sound. No stamp, no entry — こく, こく, all day long.
items.description: Means "country" or "nation"; a very common kanji seen in words for countries and citizenship, read こく in compounds and くに on its own.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、外国に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to a foreign country next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、外[がい]国[こく]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この町には外国人がたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of foreigners in this town.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]には外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]がたくさんいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の車は高いです。
example_sentences.english: Foreign cars are expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の車[くるま]は高[たか]いです。

items.mnemonic_text: Drops falling inside a window frame from the sky: rain.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the window and watch <radical>rain</radical> streak down the glass, drop by drop. Each drop lands inside its own tiny square of the frame. Rows of falling drops trapped in a frame are what we call <kanji>rain</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cow gets caught outside in the downpour and lets out a long, miserable "<reading>う</reading>ー" as the drops soak her. Every time it rains, that cow's soggy うー is the sound you hear.
items.description: Means "rain"; the base kanji for weather words and it sits on top of many other weather-related characters as a component.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日はたくさん雨が降りました。
example_sentences.english: It rained a lot yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]はたくさん雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は雨が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: I dislike rain.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は雨[あめ]が嫌[きら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は雨ですか。
example_sentences.english: Will it rain tomorrow?
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]ですか。

items.mnemonic_text: Rain (雨) with lightning stretching down: electricity.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A flash brighter than the <radical>sun</radical> tearing straight down through the <radical>rain</radical> is raw <kanji>electricity</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The lightning hits a power line and the whole street goes DEN — <reading>でん</reading> — every fluorescent tube in Koichi's konbini surging bright at once. You feel that でん in your teeth as the electricity floods back.
items.description: Means "electricity"; shows up in everyday words for trains, phones, lights, and anything electrical.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝電車で会社に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I take the train to work every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]電[でん]車[しゃ]で会[かい]社[しゃ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜に母に電話します。
example_sentences.english: I'll call my mom at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]に母[はは]に電[でん]話[わ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 暗いから電気をつけます。
example_sentences.english: It's dark, so I'll turn on the light.
example_sentences.furigana: 暗[くら]いから電[でん]気[き]をつけます。

items.mnemonic_text: A cart seen from above with an axle: a vehicle.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An axle drawn straight through a box of cargo with a wheel at either end is a <kanji>car</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A show-off racer revs his engine outside Koichi's konbini and shouts "Watch me!" He peels out so fast all you hear is a screech of "<reading>しゃ</reading>!" The vehicle vanishes down the street. Every time you see this car kanji, that "しゃ!" is the last sound it makes.
items.description: 車 and 重 are the same boxy stack, but 重 is taller and runs an extra horizontal through the middle. Count the horizontal strokes crossing the body: 重 always has one more than 車.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝電車で会社に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning I take the train to the office.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]電[でん]車[しゃ]で会[かい]社[しゃ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: あの車はとても大きいです。
example_sentences.english: That car over there is really big.
example_sentences.furigana: あの車[くるま]はとても大[おお]きいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は自転車が好きです。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother likes bikes.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]が好[す]きです。

items.mnemonic_text: A horse (馬) waiting where trains stop: a station.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A galloping <radical>horse</radical> comes charging onto the platform out of nowhere. It leaps clean over a sleeping <radical>body</radical> lying across a bench. Commuters barely look up, just another morning at the <kanji>station</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A commuter named Eki misses the last train and shouts "<reading>えき</reading>! えき!" across the empty platform, hoping the station master will hear her and hold the doors.
items.description: Means "station" — the word for a train or subway station, seen constantly in place names and on transit signs.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅は家から近いです。
example_sentences.english: The station is close to my house.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]は家[いえ]から近[ちか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員に切符を見せます。
example_sentences.english: I show my ticket to the station staff.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]に切[きっ]符[ぷ]を見[み]せます。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝この駅で電車に乗ります。
example_sentences.english: I board the train at this station every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]この駅[えき]で電[でん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]ります。

items.mnemonic_text: A neck (首) moving down a path: the road and the way.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>road</radical> narrow enough to feel like the <radical>neck</radical> of a bottle is still the only <kanji>way</kanji> through.
items.reading_mnemonic: Halfway up the road you meet a doe standing in the middle of the path, blocking the way. She won't budge, so you call out "<reading>どう</reading> do I get past you?" — and the doe just chews and stares, owning the whole road.
items.description: Means road or way; a very common kanji seen in words for streets, paths, and figurative "ways" of doing things.

example_sentences.japanese: この道は長いです。
example_sentences.english: This road is long.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は長[なが]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日道を歩きます。
example_sentences.english: I walk along the road every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]道[みち]を歩[ある]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 道の近くに公園があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a park near the road.
example_sentences.furigana: 道[みち]の近[ちか]くに公[こう]園[えん]があります。

items.mnemonic_text: A rice field (田) marked out into a town.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A farmer paces around his single square <radical>rice field</radical> every single day. Slowly other families build houses right along its edges. Soon a whole <kanji>town</kanji> surrounds that one small field.
items.reading_mnemonic: The town mayor climbs onto a soapbox in the square and announces he's the big chief now: "I'm in charge — call me <reading>ちょう</reading>!" Every time you walk into this town, you hear that same booming ちょう echoing off the buildings.
items.description: Means "town" and shows up in place names and words for local districts and neighborhoods.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は賑やかです。
